vista.gap: A is not a vista at all: it is an enclosed ruin-interior combat shot with no sky, no horizon, no moon, and no depth banding. The whole frame sits in one murky olive-grey value range (pillars, floor, fog, and characters all within roughly the same mid-dark band), so nothing recedes, there is no sense of scale beyond the arena, and the "atmosphere" reads as a single flat desaturated haze rather than layered distance. It also has no warm accent to anchor the eye; the brightest elements are the scattered white foliage specks, which pull attention randomly across the floor.
vista.fix: Re-frame the shot from outside/at the edge of the ruin with the camera low and wide behind the player so the pillars become mid-ground silhouettes, then add height/distance fog tinted to a pale sky colour with three explicit value steps (foreground near-black, mid-ground pillars ~35% grey, far ridge ~70% grey) against a lit horizon band with a large soft moon; place one warm point light (campfire or grace) in the mid-distance as the sole warm accent, and cut the scattered white foliage specks to one or two clusters so they stop competing with it.
vista.notes: B delivers the brief directly: fog-banded low-poly mountains and dead-tree silhouettes at three clear depths under a large soft moon, cool blue-grey palette tied together between sky and ground, and a single warm campfire accent giving a focal point behind the small foreground player for scale (its own weakness is the flat tan repeated grass tufts and featureless ground plane under the character).

character.gap: B's extremities are unmodified primitives: the boots are flat-ended rectangular boxes, the forearms are capped cylinders, and the legs are rigid tapered sticks with no knee or ankle bend, so the run pose reads as blocks rotated around pivots rather than a sculpted figure with articulated weight (the sword hand floats beside the hilt and the ground shadow is a smeared dark blob rather than a contact shadow, compounding the "glued primitives" read).
character.fix: Rebuild the limb extremities as tapered, bevelled meshes (wedge boot with a heel and rounded toe that tapers into a shin, forearm tapering into a wrist and mitten-style hand that actually grips the hilt), add knee and elbow joints to the rig so the run cycle bends them (front leg knee-up, trailing leg extended, arm swing counter to legs), and replace the large ground blob with a small soft-edged contact shadow under each foot.
character.notes: A's faceless hero is shaded with the same warm bounce and volumetric key light as the architecture, has a crisp grounding shadow under a weight-shifted stride, and reads as one deliberately designed silhouette against the sunlit floor rather than an assembly of parts.

combat.gap: B's arena is unbroken greybox: the ground is a single untextured olive plane with no albedo breakup, scatter, footprints or contact shadows under any of the four combatants, and the tents, crates and stakes are flat-shaded single-colour black primitives, so the fight floats on a prototype stage rather than in a camp. Compounding it, the struck enemy is a pale grey figure placed directly in front of the campfire bloom with a white burst on top, so its silhouette and recoil dissolve and the hit reads as a flash on the background, not a body taking damage.
combat.fix: Author a real ground material under the fight: a dark trampled-dirt base with a lighter snow/ash scatter mask, a ring of scuffed footprint and ember decals radiating from the campfire, and a soft contact-AO blob (roughly 1.2x foot width, 60% opacity) under every character; then darken the struck enemy's base materials to dark steel/leather (~30% value) with a thin cool rim light so it stays legible against the fire and the spark burst.
combat.notes: A reads as one coherent art direction: a unified cool-fog/ochre-grass palette with volumetric light, genuine sense of scale from the fogged giant and cliffs, and the enemy pack's hunched charging silhouettes sell a real ambush even without a hit-spark beat.

ring.gap: B's ground is a single flat navy value with no texture, no fog, and no lighting response, and the rain wall terminates on it as a hard, dead-straight horizontal line with no emissive rim or ground tint gradient; the result reads as a vertical rain-texture billboard standing on a tabletop, not a weather front rolling across terrain. Nothing in the scene is lit by the wall (the character's cape, sword, and cast shadow show zero blue-violet rim or bounce), so the threat is pasted behind the world instead of existing in it.
ring.fix: In the terrain shader, sample signed distance to the ring edge and (a) add an additive blue-violet emissive band that falls off over ~4 m from the contact line, with a darker, desaturated cold tint applied inside the ring, and (b) spawn 2-3 layers of scrolling low-fog cards with noise alpha along the base so the contact edge is broken and soft; then add a single blue-violet point/rect light parented to the nearest ring point so the player's silhouette picks up a rim highlight from the wall.
ring.notes: A's ring is rendered as translucent volumetric flame that licks through the grass and rim-lights every figure in cold blue, so the threat is physically integrated with the terrain and characters rather than layered behind them.

hud.gap: Frame B contains no HUD whatsoever — no HP/FP/stamina bars, no boss bar or name, no rune counter, no compass strip, no day/ring indicator, no lock-on reticle, no item prompt. For a piece whose entire subject is the HUD layer, it is a raw gameplay render with nothing to evaluate; the underlying environment is far more refined than A's low-poly flat-ground scene, but that is not the piece under judgement.
hud.fix: Composite the full Souls-style HUD layer over the frame before submitting: stacked HP (crimson) / FP (blue) / stamina (green) bars in dark bevelled frames with a lagging tan damage trail at top-left, a compass strip with cardinal letters at top-centre, a boss name in letterspaced serif over a hairline gold rule and a gold boss bar at bottom-centre, a rune counter with gold glyph in a dark plate at bottom-right, and a lock-on reticle on the active target.
hud.notes: A ships every element of the spec as one coherent system — charcoal bevelled frames, gold end-caps and hairline ornaments, letterspaced serif caps, a visible damage trail on the HP bar, and a lock-on reticle — with consistent gold/charcoal palette and margins so nothing reads as a default DOM widget, even though the underlying low-poly scene (flat single-value ground, placeholder boss) is far weaker than B's render.

grace.gap: B's grace emits no light into its own scene: there is no warm pool on the floor, no gold key or rim on the hooded player (who reads as a flat dark cutout), and no bounce on the surrounding stonework, so the beam reads as an unlit particle sprite composited over a uniformly murky grey-green frame; the "one warm thing in a cold world" contrast collapses into a single dark value, and the hilt-in-ground, loot, and prompt beats of the piece are absent entirely.
grace.fix: Place a warm gold point light (~2200K, ~6-8 m radius, inverse-square falloff) at floor level at the base of the grace so it lays a visible amber pool on the flagstones within ~3 m and puts a warm rim on the back of the player's hood and shoulders against the cold interior, and plant the sword-hilt mesh at that light's origin so the beam is anchored to the ground rather than hanging mid-air.
grace.notes: A delivers every beat of the brief as one coherent stylized direction: a grounded gold beam with motes that actually lights the kneeling player and the ground around it, a cold blue night with purple-rimmed ridgelines for contrast, and a rarity-coloured chest beam with a readable prompt, even though the beam core is blown out and the low-poly terrain is close to one flat value.
